entries.name: Black saxaul
entries.leaves: scale-like, reduced to cups; photosynthesis in jointed green twigs
entries.fruit: winged utricle, blown whole by wind
entries.voxel_shape: thick crooked short trunk, spongy grey bark, dense jointed green twig canopy; often the only tree for hundreds of kilometres
entries.notes: The defining tree of the cold desert: a real tree where almost nothing else woody survives. Gobi saxaul stands are routinely stripped for fuel and take decades to regrow.

entries.name: White saxaul
entries.leaves: tiny scale cups; assimilating jointed green twigs, grey-white bark
entries.voxel_shape: low crooked sand-dune tree with pendulous jointed twigs; forms open 'saxaul forests' fixed to dunes
entries.notes: The psammophyte sibling of black saxaul: where dunes move, this is the tree; Chinese afforestation leans on it heavily.

entries.name: Big sagebrush
entries.leaves: silvery grey-green, wedge-shaped with three apical lobes, aromatic
entries.fire: killed; does not resprout, reseeds slowly
entries.voxel_shape: large rounded multi-stemmed grey shrub; the default texture of the American cold-desert basin
uses: winter forage for deer and elk
entries.notes: Covers millions of hectares of the Great Basin; where it grows over a metre tall the soil is usually arable. Fire removes it wholesale and recovery takes decades.

entries.name: Great Basin bristlecone pine
entries.leaves: five-needle fascicles, deep green with white stomatal band, needles held 40+ years
entries.flowers: conifer cones; purple female cones with bristle-tipped scales
entries.fruit: winged pine seeds, dispersed by Clark's nutcrackers
entries.voxel_shape: short gnarled wind-carved pine, mostly dead-looking twisted wood with a few living strips; foxtail-like needle bottlebrushes
entries.notes: The oldest non-clonal organisms alive (Methuselah, ~4,800 years). Grows only on cold dry high ridges above the Great Basin; an ideal landmark for very high cold country.

entries.name: Singleleaf piñon
entries.leaves: single stout needle per bundle, blue-green
entries.fruit: large edible piñon nut (one seed per scale)
entries.voxel_shape: broad round-crowned small pine, open and crooked; the pie-shaped canopy over the piñon-juniper belt
entries.notes: The edible-nut pine of the Colorado Plateau and Great Basin; piñon-juniper woodland is the transition band between cold desert and forest.

entries.name: Utah juniper
entries.leaves: scale-like grey-green, pressed to twigs
entries.flowers: conifer; berry-like cones on separate trees
entries.fruit: bluish berry-like cone, used as spice and gin flavouring
entries.voxel_shape: rounded dense-crowned evergreen small tree with fibrous red-grey bark; often in pure stands on shallow rocky soils
entries.notes: The other half of the piñon-juniper belt; junipers are famously long-lived and deep-rooted on near-bare rock.

entries.name: Shadscale
entries.leaves: silver-grey, round, densely scaly
entries.fruit: two-winged flat bract enclosing the seed (a floating disc)
entries.voxel_shape: low dense silver dome, often in pure stands on salt-affected clay pans
entries.notes: The salt-loving silver dome of the lowest, driest basins; where shadscale dominates, the soil is too alkaline for sagebrush.

entries.name: Fourwing saltbush
entries.leaves: narrow grey-green, scaly, paired
entries.fruit: utricle enclosed in four broad papery wings
entries.voxel_shape: rounded grey-green shrub with characteristic four-winged pale fruits dangling in late summer
entries.notes: A workhorse of arid land restoration: it fixes atmospheric nitrogen poorly but tolerates alkali that kills almost everything else.

entries.name: Black greasewood
entries.leaves: narrow succulent green, falling in winter, spines at branch tips
entries.fruit: dry, spirally-winged achene in a fleshy bladdery bract
entries.voxel_shape: dark rounded thicket with upright spiny branches; a half-dead-looking succulent shrub with deep roots to the water table
uses: indicator of high water table / saline flats
forage (sheep and goats eat the leaves, horses can be poisoned)
entries.notes: The dark ring-marker of alkaline flats where groundwater is near the surface; its presence means drilling there can hit brackish water.

entries.name: Rubber rabbitbrush
entries.leaves: narrow grey, densely fuzzy, rubbery latex when crushed
entries.flowers: masses of small golden yellow heads, late summer-autumn
entries.voxel_shape: bright green rounded shrub that flares gold in late summer; first thing back after a burn
entries.notes: The torch of disturbed cold-desert ground: after fire it erupts in gold and dominates the first years before sagebrush returns.

entries.name: Winterfat
entries.leaves: woolly white-grey, entire, erect stems
entries.voxel_shape: low silvery woolly tuft; looks frosted even in summer heat
entries.notes: Named for its value: stock fatten on it in winter when everything else is straw. One of the plants range scientists most want to see reseeded.

entries.name: Basin wildrye
entries.leaves: broad blue-green blades with coarse veins
entries.voxel_shape: tall coarse bunchgrass in dense colonies along swales and dry lake beds
entries.notes: The tallest native grass of the sagebrush zone; swales full of wildrye mark where the shallow water table lives.

entries.name: Gobi feather grass
entries.leaves: narrow inrolled blades, stiff, greyish
entries.flowers: feathery awns up to 20 cm, rippling in wind, summer
entries.fruit: awned caryopsis that drills itself into soil
entries.voxel_shape: open tussocks whose long silvery awns flow like smoke over the stony desert
entries.notes: The Gobi's signature grass: in wind the awns make the whole steppe shimmer. Associated with the Anabasis-Saxaul desert communities.

entries.name: Needle-and-thread grass
entries.leaves: very narrow, inrolled, grey-green
entries.flowers: very long twisting awns (10-20 cm), early summer
entries.voxel_shape: fine feathery tussocks rippling white; awns curl and untwist with humidity
uses: hypothesis test: awns drill seeds into soil
entries.notes: Its awned seeds can injure livestock eyes and mouths when cured — a real rangeland hazard worth modelling as a wound source.

entries.name: Squirreltail
entries.leaves: narrow, often curling, blue-green
entries.flowers: bottlebrush spike with long divergent awns, late spring
entries.voxel_shape: short tufts with a distinctive bottlebrush tail of bristles held aloft
entries.notes: The ecological first responder of the Intermountain West: appears after fire or overgrazing and holds the soil while shrubs re-establish.

entries.name: Mormon tea
entries.leaves: none — jointed leafless green stems, like tiny bamboo
entries.flowers: tiny scale-covered; cones on separate plants
entries.voxel_shape: wiry bright-green jointed broom from a woody base; a leafless bush of straight segmented wands
entries.notes: A gymnosperm hiding in plain sight: no leaves at all, just photosynthetic stems. Early settlers brewed a stimulating tea from it.

entries.name: Spiny hopsage
entries.leaves: grey-green, rounded, turning pinkish in autumn
entries.voxel_shape: tangled grey spiny thicket studded with papery inflated pinkish seed pods
entries.notes: Looks dead half the year, then flushes pale pink bracts; one of the few cold-desert shrubs with showy autumn colour.

entries.name: Antelope bitterbrush
entries.leaves: wedge-shaped three-lobed, dark green above, white-woolly below
entries.fruit: dry achenes with style attached, persisting
entries.voxel_shape: rounded dense shrub; in spring a cream-yellow haze, otherwise dark and woolly
uses: critical deer and antelope winter browse
entries.notes: The shrub mule deer will walk past sagebrush to reach; stands have been declining as cheatgrass outcompetes it after fire.

entries.name: Saltgrass
entries.leaves: stiff two-ranked blades, salt crystals on blades
entries.voxel_shape: flat stoloniferous mats, blue-green with a white salt frost; the lawn of alkaline flats
entries.notes: Spreads by stolons across alkali crusts where nothing else grows; the obvious plant for revegetating bare salt pans in-game.

entries.name: Mountain snowberry
entries.leaves: small oval, dark blue-green, opposite
entries.fruit: bright white waxy berry that persists into winter
entries.voxel_shape: lanky suckering bush, plain green in summer, dotted white with berries all winter
entries.notes: The white dots on an otherwise winter-bare bush give it away; borders washes and swales in cold-desert country.

entries.name: Leafless calligonum (sha-guai-zao)
entries.leaves: tiny linear leaves falling early; jointed green twigs assimilate
entries.fruit: globose with 4-8 winged ribs, turns yellow then purple
entries.voxel_shape: flexuous grey-green wands; tumbles of wiry branches over sand dunes with corky winged fruits
entries.notes: The other great dune-fixer of Central Asia alongside saxaul; its corky winged fruits skitter across the sand like dry seedpods.

entries.name: Salt anabasis (biyurgun)
entries.leaves: fleshy, awl-shaped then scale-like; cushion of jointed glaucous stems
entries.voxel_shape: low tight grey-green cushion of stubby jointed fingers on saline clay pans
uses: winter camel forage (the main camel plant of the clay deserts)
entries.notes: The camel's winter lifeline on solonchak clays — vast Ustyurt plateaus are dominated by it. Unpalatable to cattle; camels only.

entries.name: Caspian kalidium
entries.leaves: tuberculate, undeveloped, fused to jointed stems; succulent
entries.flowers: segments fused into fleshy pentagonal cups, July-August
entries.voxel_shape: fleshy glasswort-like mat of pale jointed stems on salt-lake shores and solonchaks
entries.notes: A salicornia-like halophyte of salt-lake margins; carpeting the shores of Caspian and Aral basin pans.

entries.name: Nitre bush (shixiang)
entries.leaves: thick fleshy, grey-green, spoon-shaped
entries.fruit: red sour-sweet fleshy drupe ('Gobi cherry'), eaten fresh and dried
entries.voxel_shape: dense spiny grey-green shrub laden with red dates in late summer; classic takyr-edge plant
entries.notes: The Gobi's fruit tree: its red 'black wolfberry' is sold dried and is one of the few edible wild fruits of the true desert.

entries.name: Korshinski peashrub
entries.leaves: pinnate, small leaflets, bright green
entries.voxel_shape: upright spiny pea-flower shrub; in May a yellow-flowered hedge across stabilized dunes
entries.notes: The Chinese Academy's favourite sand-stabilizer in Ningxia and Inner Mongolia; a nitrogen-fixer that turns moving dunes into anchored scrub.

entries.name: Mongolian allium
entries.leaves: narrow cylindrical hollow leaves, onion-scented
entries.voxel_shape: low clumps of wiry onion leaves with purple pom-pom umbels on thin stalks
entries.notes: A fragrant onion of the desert-steppe; when it flowers the Gobi smells faintly of leeks after rain.

entries.name: Multi-root allium (grassland chive)
entries.leaves: many basal linear leaves from a large clumping rhizome
entries.flowers: purple umbels on leafless scapes, July
entries.voxel_shape: dense rhizomatous clumps of chive-like leaves; one root mass can hold dozens of tufts
uses: forage (key winter fodder in Inner Mongolia)
entries.notes: The true 'chive' of the Asian drylands; its rhizome mats anchor takyr micro-knolls and feed sheep through winter.

entries.name: Frigid wormwood
entries.leaves: finely dissected silky silver leaves, sweet-scented
entries.voxel_shape: low silvery spreading mounds; the soft grey counterpoint to spiny desert shrubs
entries.notes: Indicator of healthy desert-steppe under light grazing; heavy grazing converts its ground to bare soil and unpalatable weeds.

entries.name: Russian salt tree
entries.leaves: pinnate compound, blue-green, spine-tipped twigs
entries.flowers: pink to lilac pea-flowers, May-June, showy
entries.voxel_shape: upright spiny legume shrub; pink-flowered haze over saline stream margins
entries.notes: One of the showiest shrubs of Central Asian salt pans — lilac flowers against white crust; planted as a windbreak in salinized districts.

entries.name: Ma huang (Chinese ephedra)
entries.leaves: none — jointed green stems like tiny horsetail
entries.voxel_shape: low wiry mats of segmented yellow-green wands on arid loess
entries.notes: The original source of ephedrine, used in China for thousands of years; overharvested in the wild for pharmaceutical supply.

entries.name: Neneo
entries.leaves: trifid, rigid, spine-tipped, resinous and pungent when crushed
entries.voxel_shape: round dense cushion of pale thorns; looks like a soft green pincushion but is razor sharp
uses: fuel (burns hot; used for signal fires)
entries.notes: Patagonia's signature cold-desert shrub: knee-high cushions of triple thorns stretching to the horizon; guanaco country.

entries.name: Yareta (llareta)
entries.leaves: minute densely packed rosettes forming a hemispherical mat
entries.voxel_shape: huge chartreuse hemispherical mound up to 6 m across; a rock-like cushion of living resin, one of the highest-elevation woody plants on Earth
entries.notes: The eternal cushion: 3,000-year-old mats at 4,000-5,200 m in the Atacama Puna. Heavily protected now; never show it as fuel-gatherable.

entries.name: Snow lotus (tian shan xue lian)
entries.leaves: silvery-white woolly rosette pressed to the ground
entries.flowers: purple florets hidden among woolly bracts, July-August
entries.voxel_shape: small silver rosette glowing against black rock at the snow line; denser and rounder than any alpine edelweiss
uses: prized traditional Chinese medicine ('qi and blood')
entries.notes: A high-cold legend of the Tien Shan and Altai; its silver rosettes are gathered to extinction where accessible. Model it rare and far from trails.

entries.name: Awned haircap moss (desert moss)
entries.leaves: awned, twisted-crisp when dry, unfurling green when wet
entries.voxel_shape: black-green turf that looks dead dust until rain; the most famous desiccation-tolerant plant on Earth
entries.notes: Survives near-total desiccation, -196 C liquid nitrogen and years without water; the Gobi's resurrection moss and a model for Mars botany.

entries.name: Biological soil crust (desert varnish crust)
entries.latin: Collema spp. with Syntrichia spp. and cyanobacteria
entries.leaves: none; dark crinkled foliose lichens over cyanobacterial filaments
entries.fire: destroyed; takes decades to centuries to recover
entries.voxel_shape: near-black bumpy rind on bare fines between shrubs; the ground's own skin
entries.notes: The living skin of cold-desert soil: crushes under a boot print for a lifetime. Any game that lets players strip it is simulating real desertification.
